prompt: Create a transparent Pocket Dungeon pixel-art atlas with EXACTLY THREE EQUAL COLUMNS x ONE ROW, in this order: RIGHT edge profile, LEFT edge profile, REAR edge profile, for the same square club-carpet edge-transition floor tile. Use the supplied contact to identify the source tile and materials. Camera must be axis-aligned straight-on at the side of each horizontal floor tile, a true orthographic edge elevation, no perspective and no isometric angle. Each silhouette is a very thin horizontal slab edge, about 6 to 7 times wider than its height, matching the existing accepted FRONT edge elevation proportions. Do not show the broad upper carpet surface or any top-down diamond pattern; show only the narrow vertical outer edge and physical thickness. Direction-specific source identity from the top plan: the RIGHT-facing edge is continuous brown hardwood across its full length (all wood); the LEFT-facing edge is continuous red rug cloth across its full length (all carpet); the REAR-facing edge is a mixed edge with the brown hardwood strip at the opposite endpoint from the FRONT (wood at the left endpoint, carpet cloth across the rest). Crisp clustered pixel art, dark outlines, red carpet backing edge, brown plank grain where wood is exposed, gold trim only where source has binding. Transparent outside each thin profile; no extra panels, patches, labels, detached guide marks, bolts or generic tray.
